newsitem.title: USA: Wasatch affiliate finalizes Kiwi Intl bid.
newsitem.headline: Wasatch affiliate finalizes Kiwi Intl bid.

text.p: Wasatch International Corp said Friday its Edwards-Wasatch Enterprises LLC affiliate has finalized plans for a $16.5 million bid to buy Kiwi International Air Lines.
Privately held Kiwi has been in Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings since September 1996.

Wasatch president Joe Logan Jr said in a press release the bid would resolve all creditors' obligations, curtail all adminstrative proceedings and expenses and would streamline Edwards-Wasatch's ability, through a newly formed holding company, to provide its management control through ownership.

Edwards-Wasatch has already advonced Kiwi more than $10 million in cash and letters of credit, the company said. But it was not feasible to make further investments without full management control through ownership, it said.
Logan said the purchase eliminates the need for a Plan of Arrangement and permits Kiwi to continue to operate without interruption on an expanded basis.
Logan said Kiwi would expand its cargo and charter businesses. The airline will expand its fleet, too, he said.
Logan said bankruptcy proceedings should be finished in July, and ownership will be transferred to Edwards-Wasatch then.
Kiwi resumed flying Jan. 20 after suspending flights Oct. 15 as part of its bankruptcy proceedings.
At its peak, the airline had 15 aircraft and 1,200 employees.
